titlePlain: Metrics That Actually Matter: Qubit Count, Fidelity,
subtitle: Lesson 24 · Comparing Hardware Platforms

steps.sub: Qubit-count headlines read like a clock-speed race — it isn't one

steps.label: Count ≠ quality
steps.sub: A noisy, poorly-connected qubit contributes close to nothing useful

steps.label: 1,000 bad > 50 good?
steps.sub: Not necessarily — a smaller, well-connected, high-fidelity device can win

steps.label: Single-qubit gate
steps.sub: Usually the highest fidelity on the chip, often 99.9%+

steps.label: Two-qubit gate
steps.sub: Almost always noticeably worse — the limiting number for most circuits

steps.label: Readout fidelity
steps.sub: Great gates, bad readout — still a circuit that gives garbage answers

eyebrow: The rule that ties it together

steps.label: Enough coherent depth
steps.sub: To execute the full gate sequence before noise destroys it — and

steps.label: Enough connectivity
steps.sub: To route it without exploding that depth with SWAPs

subtitle: Can you fold qubit count, fidelity, and connectivity into one number? Several vendors have tried.
